detail.text:
**Summary for the operator**

The noon report nr-0106 for MV TORMAR SPRING has been fully checked. The reported speed of 12.5 kn differs from the 9.6 kn implied by the 231.3 nm run over 24 h, but the report's remarks explain it: the main engine stopped 0610–1140 UTC (5.5 h) for fuel oil filters choked with sludge, and speed is given over the remaining 18.5 h of steaming — voyage agent confirmed the stoppage agrees with the report, so nothing is asked of the Master on that point. The Master's ETA of 31 January 2025 11:00 UTC for Sept-Îles is consistent with the distance to go at the reported speed, and no charter party ETA notice is due now (the next falls due at 3 days before arrival). Fuel consumption of 18.8 t VLSFO is within the CP warranty of 24 t per day, so nothing needs to be sent on performance.

A decision is yours: whether to put MV TORMAR SPRING off hire for the 26 January engine stop (0610–1140 UTC, 5.5 hours). The CP off-hire clause covers loss of time from breakdown of machinery, though the owner may argue the cause was fuel supplied by the charterer — that claim is yours to make if you proceed. If you say yes, I will draft an email to the owner's vessel technical management giving the period and reason and asking for the engine log extract, and propose the off-hire entry in the voyage management system.

Dear Sirs,

We write to notify you that MV TORMAR SPRING was off hire for a main-engine stop on 2025-01-26T06:10–11:40 UTC (5.5 hours). The stoppage was caused by fuel oil filters choked with sludge stirred up in heavy weather. The filters were cleaned and the engine restarted.

Hire ceases for this period per the CP off-hire clause. VLSFO 1.1 t used during the stoppage (generators and boiler) is for the owner's account.

Please provide the engine log extract for the stop.

Kind regards,
Operations
